//Kestrel: gRPC requires HTTP/2. Over TLS the client and server negotiate it with ALPN,
but there is no TLS here (service-to-service inside the compose network), so
there is nothing to negotiate with -- the protocol has to be stated up front.
Kestrel's default of Http1AndHttp2 on a plaintext port is exactly the ambiguous
case, so gRPC gets its own port pinned to Http2 and REST keeps 8080 on Http1.
In production you would terminate TLS at the ingress (Istio, in this repo's
chart/) and this split would collapse back into one port.
